messages.subject: probe2WayMC std.lv=TRUE/FALSE
parts:
Hi all,

I have three continuous latent variables and I tested a moderation. The product term was created with indProd - doubleMC = T.

I would like to ask you one question:

When std.lv=TRUE, and so when the variance is fixed and the first indicator of each latent variable is free, the slopes of the predictor (using probe2WayMC) at three levels of the moderator (1 SD above the mean, 0, 1 SD below the mean), are much more different than when std.lv=FALSE. 
I have to explain this to my supervisors and I am not sure what to tell them. Would it be correct just simply saying that it depends on the how the variance of the latents is treated, which in turn affects the variance of the simple slope? 


 Many thanks.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: probe2WayMC std.lv=TRUE/FALSE
parts: Different methods of scale setting result in different parameter estimates and different standard errors (for details you can see: https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/1082-989X.6.3.258). Given that the simple slopes (and their standard errors) are functions of the model parameters it makes sense that these would be different.
